title: Limit home purchases by foreigners in the Canaries
detail: Changes in the national parliament to limit home buying by foreigners in the Canary Islands. They would be based on the islands' special EU status as an outermost region (*región ultraperiférica*, RUP) and follow EU law. Also EU and national changes to allow a Canary Islands residence law (*Ley Canaria de Residencia*) to control population growth. The programme does not say who exactly or what limits.
c: Limiting home buying by EU citizens is not possible, because of the EU rules on free movement of money and the freedom to settle. In our estimate, only a few countries have exceptions, under special agreements added to the EU treaties. RUP status (art. 349 TFEU) allows some changes to EU rules, but such a limit would need a decision by the EU Council and would be challenged. We rate it C, not D, because the programme does not say whether EU citizens would be included.

title: Rules for holiday rentals where housing is under pressure
detail: A national and EU legal basis so the Canary Islands and their town halls can limit tourist use of homes (*vivienda vacacional*) where they can prove pressure on housing. The rules would separate owners who rent now and then from professional owners who rent all the time.
c: The Canary Islands already passed a law on holiday rentals (Ley 6/2025). A national framework is realistic.
pos: The islands could limit holiday rentals where they push local people out.
neg: Owners of holiday rentals earn less, and there may be disputes under EU law.

s.t: Canary Islands Ley 6/2025 on holiday lets (BOE)

title: Stable rentals: tax breaks for small landlords
detail: Better state tax breaks for small landlords who join affordable rental schemes (*alquiler asequible*), with public guarantees against unpaid rent and damage. Money for renovating empty homes would depend on joining those schemes. The programme says nothing about rent limits.
c: The tax breaks are realistic and not expensive.
pos: Small landlords become more willing to rent at affordable prices.
neg: It costs the state money, and some of the help goes to people who would rent out their homes anyway.

title: Tax breaks on La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro
detail: Keep the 60% income tax (*IRPF*) deduction for La Palma and extend it to La Gomera and El Hierro. Also a 50% cut in the social security fees employers pay (*bonificación de cuotas*) on these three islands.
c: Tax breaks for La Palma after the volcano already apply. Extending them is cheap.
pos: It helps islands hit by the volcano and by people moving away.
neg: The state loses tax money, and people may register falsely on the islands.

title: Protect and update the Canary Islands tax regime (*REF*)
detail: Keep and update the special economic and tax system (*Régimen Económico y Fiscal de Canarias*, REF), which makes up for the islands' permanent disadvantages. REF money should not count as normal funding for health, education and social services. No changes by the state without the islands' agreement.
c: The Constitution (third additional provision) and the Statute of Autonomy protect the REF. Updating it is normal.
pos: The islands keep getting help with the extra costs of island life.
neg: The system costs the state tax money. In our estimate, some of the tax breaks (the special economic zone *ZEC* and the investment reserve *RIC*) mostly help large companies.

s.t: Ley 19/1994 on the Canary Islands economic and tax regime, REF (BOE)

title: Share new migrants between regions automatically
detail: When a region where migrants first arrive goes over set limits, people would move to other regions (*comunidades autónomas*) automatically, without talks about each case. This needs changes to the law.
c: RDL 2/2025 already made sharing between regions compulsory. Several regions are challenging it at the Constitutional Court.
pos: Regions share the work of receiving migrants.
neg: Regions get duties without agreeing to them, which leads to disputes about powers at the Constitutional Court.

s.t: BOE: Madrid's challenge at the Constitutional Court to RDL 2/2025 on distributing migrant minors

title: Keep the 75% travel discount for residents
detail: Keep the 75% discount on flights and ferries for residents, watch for prices raised on purpose, protect direct links between the smaller islands, and make the state pay 100% of the real cost of the help for shipping goods.
c: The REF sets the 75% discount, and keeping it is realistic. In our estimate it costs about €600 to 700 million a year.
pos: Affordable travel between the islands and to mainland Spain.
neg: Part of the discount may end up in higher prices.

s.t: Ley 19/1994 on the Canary Islands economic and tax regime, REF (BOE)
